info.desc: AM is the fifth studio album by the English indie rock band Arctic Monkeys. It was released on 9 September 2013 in Europe, 6 September 2013 in Australia, and 10 September 2013 in the United States. On 15 July 2013, the album cover artwork was revealed. The album features the singles: "R U Mine?", "Do I Wanna Know?", "Why'd You Only Call Me When You're High?", "Arabella", "One For The Road" and "Snap Out of It". It also features guest appearances by Josh Homme, Bill Ryder-Jones and Pete Thomas. It was produced by James Ford and co-produced by Ross Orton .

podcast.body: Considered by a significant portion of critics in Europe, and NME and El Rhino Nido magazines, as one of the band's best albums, almost on par with "Humbug," receiving 10/10 ratings. In Europe, it was a Top 5 album in nearly all publications for its year. However, in the United States, some critics viewed it as a "superstar" album that didn't contribute much creatively. "Aquí en Europa el AEM está considerado también uno de los mejores álbumes de los Artic Monkeys casi a nivel del Amburg, de hecho NEM. La propia revista NEM y el Rino Nido le daban 10 sobre 10."

podcast.body: This album, described as their latest at the time of discussion, marked the first instance the band worked with a major professional producer, Josh Homme, known for his work with Queens of the Stone Age. This collaboration elevated Arctic Monkeys' music to an unprecedented level of quality, making "AM" a rock masterpiece. The professional production helped to refine many of the subtle production flaws that the band had made in previous albums by deliberately avoiding industry influence. "El elyem es una obra maestra con un nivel de calidad de rock increíble y en parte gracias a que pule muchos de esos pequeños efectos de producción, que la banda lejos de querer influenciarse por la industria había ido cometiendo en sus iscos anteriores."
